messages:
diego-newhire: hey team 👋 quick onboarding questions after orientation — 1) my offer says relocation reimbursement up to $5k but HR portal says it might be taxable. Is that true if paid via payroll? 2) Im moving to Spain next month for a 6-month project  does that affect benefits eligibility / medical coverage? 3) if I end up eligible for COBRA when I return, whats the window and who to contact?

nina-peopleops: welcome @diego-newhire! short answers: (1) relocation reimbursements paid through payroll are typically taxable as income. We can sometimes issue a vendor reimbursement (non-payroll) for certain relocation vendors which is non-taxable. Please submit receipts to expenses with code "relocation-reimb" and include vendor invoices; we'll triage.

linda-payroll: FYI: if reimbursement goes through payroll it will show as Other Compensation and be subject to applicable taxes. If we can route to AP/vendor payment we avoid payroll tax but it depends on vendor type and service date. DM the receipts and invoice names and we can advise.

diego-newhire: thx — I have movers and lease deposit receipts. If we do vendor route who pays the vendor directly? Also on benefits: Im on the company PPO and wondered if it covers international care or if I should buy short-term travel health?

nina-peopleops: we can pay international movers via AP (vendor) if you provide the vendor W-9/foreign equivalent + invoice. For lease deposit we usually reimburse the employee via expense (taxable) unless landlord invoices Redwood directly. We'll confirm per-case.

visa-bot: Note: international assignment may affect benefits eligibility depending on payroll locus and local entity rules. If you remain on US payroll and are a US benefits-eligible employee, your Redwood medical plan can provide international emergency care but not routine local coverage. Short-term travel insurance is recommended for routine local care.

diego-newhire: OK, that helps. COBRA Q: whats the timeline if I leave US payroll or go on unpaid LOA?

nina-peopleops: COBRA basics: 60-day election window from qualifying event date/notice. Coverage retro to loss of coverage date if elected. For US-entity employees who terminate or lose coverage while abroad, COBRA still applies if the plan is subject to COBRA. We'll open ticket BEN-4701 to confirm your plan's COBRA applicability for international assignments.

linda-payroll: also note: if you go on local Spanish payroll (i.e., transferred to local entity) you may lose US benefits and would be eligible for COBRA. If you remain on US payroll but on an unpaid LOA we assess eligibility case-by-case.

diego-newhire: awesome. last one: commuter/pre-tax transit — I wont use it while abroad. do I need to unenroll to avoid deductions?

nina-peopleops: yes please change commuter elections in Workday before payroll cutoff to stop deductions. If you miss cutoff we can process a delta payroll correction but better to update proactively. Commuter refunds are handled by the vendor and may take 1-2 cycles.

relocation-team: @diego-newhire filing: relocation ticket REL-2145 opened. Please upload invoices & vendor tax docs to Workday under "Relocation" and tag this ticket. We'll route vendor-payable items to AP where possible to avoid payroll taxation.

diego-newhire: thanks everyone 60a i'll upload docs now and watch BEN-4701 and REL-2145. appreciate the help :thumbsup:
